briefFidelity: FAIL, and this alone settles it. The brief asks for an arcade: repeated bays seen head on, the rhythm of supports, the same member restated at descending scale and nested inward, with one warm accent marking the innermost bay. Before reading it I described radial rosettes - centred emblems built by rotating translucent triangles, squares and discs around a point. Rotation is not repetition of bays, and a starburst has no interval. Nothing in the twelve reads as a colonnade, a run, a support, or a load path; the closest a seed comes is 10622's concentric triangles and 9906/10085's inscribed circles, which are nesting without members and without rhythm. The accent placement is inverted: the brief puts the warm hue at the innermost bay, and in 9190, 9548 and 10980 the orange sits on the OUTERMOST satellites, flung to the perimeter. Only the palette instruction is honoured - iron and ash over near-black is exactly what is there. The other correct read is 'engineered rather than drawn', which the work fails from the other side: 9190 and 9548 read as snowflake and flower, decorative rather than structural, and 9727 is a chaotic confetti scatter with no centre at all, which is the opposite of load-bearing.
seedVariation: Mixed, and failing in both directions at once. Shared identity is present and strong - same alpha compositing, same palette, same centred construction across all twelve. But at 120px the set collapses into four or five families rather than twelve works: 9011, 10622, 10801 and 10443 are near-interchangeable grey right-pointing wedges; 9369, 9906 and 10085 are three grey discs; 9190, 10264 and 10980 are one orange starburst at three spreads. Meanwhile 9727 has drifted off-model entirely and shares only the palette. So the variation that exists is between families, not within them, and one member sits outside the family system.
thumbnailSurvival: It reads, but not as twelve things. The silhouettes are clean and the near-black ground holds them, so nothing turns to mush at 120px except 9727. The orange accent is the single most legible identifier, and the seeds lacking it - four grey triangles and three grey discs - converge on one dim shape. 9369 is the worst case: its value sits so close to the ground that at browse size it is a smudge rather than an object, and it is also the seed chosen for the 512px hero, where it is still murky and uncomposed.
marketResponse: Visible, but it is not the change the brief claimed, and that is the second independent failure. The brief asks for members to be LOST and the interval to WIDEN under drawdown, and for the colonnade to FILL BACK IN with nesting DEEPENING in recovery - a change in count and spacing. What actually happens is a change in scale and opacity: under stress the satellite ring expands outward, the shapes grow, edges lighten and the central mass hollows out. Member count does not visibly drop - 9190 under stress carries the same population pushed further out, and 9548's perimeter squares get LARGER and more saturated, which is structure gaining weight, not shedding it. Recovery is not a deepening; it is a return to something close to neutral. Legibility is also uneven: the transformation is clear on 9190 and 9548 at 256px but marginal on 9011 and nearly absent on 9369, and at true browse size the latter two would show no state at all.
tokenIdentity: Holds. Across all four seeds on the states sheet the object is unmistakably the same object in all three rows - same palette, same symmetry order, same silhouette family, same primitive vocabulary. Nothing morphs into a different work under stress. This is the one axis the piece passes cleanly.
composition: Centred emblem with satellites, and the hierarchy works where the density is moderate: 9011, 9906, 10085 and 10622 have a clear dominant mass and a legible ground. It breaks at both extremes. 9727 has no focal point at all, just scattered squares and small triangles with the centre vacated. 9369 and the 512px hero are so low in contrast against the black that the form barely separates from the ground, and the small pale squares on the disc read as random placement rather than composition. Clipping is real and uncontrolled: 9190 and 9548 are cut at the top and bottom edges, and 10980's satellites run to the frame corners and are severed there, reading as debris rather than as a bounded work.
reasoning: My stage-1 description, written with no knowledge of the brief, called this 'layered vector rosettes' and 'translucent primitive mandalas' built by rotating shapes around a centre. The brief asked for an arcade - a flattened colonnade whose subject is interval and weight, the same member restated at descending scale, nested inward, with the warm accent at the innermost bay. Those are not the same object and no amount of squinting reconciles them: rotational symmetry replaced repeated bays, satellites replaced supports, and the accent ended up on the outside instead of the inside. The market response fails independently, because the brief specified a change in member COUNT and INTERVAL and what ships is a change in SCALE and OPACITY - stress makes the structure bigger and paler when it was asked to make it sparser and wider. The palette is right and token identity across the three conditions is solid, and on its own terms several seeds are handsome, but brief fidelity is a gate and this misses the subject of the brief rather than its execution. Add that the twelve resolve into four or five families at browse size, that 9727 is off-model, that three seeds clip at the frame, and that the chosen hero is the murkiest image in the set, and this is not a work to commit permanently on chain.
wouldChange: Rebuild the geometry around the actual subject: replace rotation-about-a-centre with a run of repeated bays - the same member profile restated at descending scale and nested inward - so that interval and weight, not radial symmetry, are what the eye reads; put the warm accent on the innermost bay only; and rebind market state to member COUNT and spacing (bays removed and the interval widened under drawdown, refilled and deepened in recovery) instead of to the scale and opacity of a satellite ring.
